integrationsCron.recurringJobsRunByPgCron: Recurring jobs run by pg_cron inside Postgres. Schedules use GMT unless cron.timezone says otherwise.
integrationsCron.name: Name
integrationsCron.itStopsRunningItsRunHistory: It stops running. Its run history stays in cron.job_run_details.
integrationsCron.jobsRunInsidePostgresAsThe: Jobs run inside Postgres as the user that scheduled them.
integrationsCron.renamingReplacesTheJobWithA: Renaming replaces the job with a new one.
integrationsCron.aCronExpressionMinuteHourDay: A cron expression: minute hour day month weekday.
integrationsCron.functionsWithoutArgumentsOutsideSupabase: Functions without arguments, outside Supabase's schemas.
integrationsCron.enableItUnderDatabaseExtensionsFirst: Enable it under Database › Extensions first.
integrationsCron.httpJobsNeedThePgNet: HTTP jobs need the pg_net extension
integrationsCron.aJsonObjectJobsAreStored: A JSON object. Jobs are stored in plain text in cron.job, so avoid putting secrets here; read them from Vault in a SQL job instead.

integrationsDataApiDocs.postgrestMayHaveItsOpenapiOutput: PostgREST may have its OpenAPI output turned off (PGRST_OPENAPI_MODE), or the stack may be down.
integrationsDataApiDocs.couldnTReadTheDataApi: Couldn't read the Data API's description: {{message}}
integrationsDataApiDocs.signUsersUpAndInAnd: Sign users up and in, and manage the signed-in user, with Supabase Auth.
integrationsDataApiDocs.itMayHaveBeenRenamedOr: It may have been renamed or removed, or not be exposed to API roles.
integrationsDataApiDocs.name: Name
integrationsDataApiDocs.everyTableAndViewInThe: Every table and view in the exposed schema gets REST endpoints. Row Level Security decides which rows each user can read and change.
integrationsDataApiDocs.noTablesOrViewsAreExposed: No tables or views are exposed.
integrationsDataApiDocs.stableFunctionsCanAlsoBeCalled: Stable functions can also be called with GET and the arguments in the query string.
integrationsDataApiDocs.volatileFunctionsCanOnlyBeCalled: Volatile functions can only be called with POST.
integrationsDataApiDocs.postgresFunctionsInTheExposedSchema: Postgres functions in the exposed schema can be called as remote procedures, with their arguments as JSON.
integrationsDataApiDocs.fromTheDataApiSOwn: from the Data API's own description
integrationsDataApiDocs.theDataApiTurnsTheExposed: The Data API turns the exposed schema into a REST API with PostgREST. These docs are written from that API's own description, so they follow your tables, views and functions.
integrationsDataApiDocs.installSupabaseJsAndCreateA: Install supabase-js and create a client with the project URL and its public key.
integrationsDataApiDocs.safeInABrowserWhenRow: Safe in a browser when Row Level Security is on.
integrationsDataApiDocs.theSupabaseCliCanWriteTypescript: The Supabase CLI can write TypeScript types for your schema straight from the database. Pass them to {{call}} to type every query.
integrationsDataApiDocs.supermixerReadsTheDescriptionWithThe: Supermixer reads the description with the service role, so it lists everything that role can reach. The anon and authenticated roles may see less, depending on their privileges (Database › Column Privileges) and Row Level Security. Only the stack's default exposed schema is described.
integrationsDataApiDocs.everyRequestNamesAKeyWhich: Every request names a key. Which key, and whether a user is signed in, decides what Postgres role the request runs as.
integrationsDataApiDocs.theAnonOrPublishableKeyIs: The anon or publishable key is meant for browsers and apps. Requests run as the anon role until a user signs in, then as authenticated. Turn on Row Level Security for every exposed table.
integrationsDataApiDocs.aSignedInUserSAccess: A signed-in user's access token goes in the Authorization header instead of the key. Policies can read who they are with auth.uid().
integrationsDataApiDocs.theServiceRoleBypassesRowLevel: The service role bypasses Row Level Security. Keep its key on servers, never in a browser or app. Members who may see it find it in <link>Project Settings › API Keys</link>.

integrationsGraphiql.queryTheDatabaseWithGraphqlThrough: Query the database with GraphQL through pg_graphql. Queries run as the database user Supermixer connects with, so Row Level Security doesn't limit them.
integrationsGraphiql.createsTheGraphqlSchemaTheApi: Creates the graphql schema. The API's /graphql/v1 endpoint then serves the same schema to your apps, following their roles and policies.
integrationsGraphiql.noTablesAreExposedToGraphql: No tables are exposed to GraphQL. pg_graphql shows tables in the schemas on the search path.
integrationsGraphiql.yourRoleCanOnlyRunQueries: Your role can only run queries, not mutations.

integrations.scheduleRecurringJobsInPostgresSql: Schedule recurring jobs in Postgres: SQL, database functions or HTTP requests.
integrations.durableMessageQueuesInPostgresWith: Durable message queues in Postgres with guaranteed delivery, using pgmq.
integrations.storeSecretsEncryptedInTheDatabase: Store secrets encrypted in the database and read them from SQL.
integrations.sendAnHttpRequestWhenRows: Send an HTTP request when rows are inserted, updated or deleted.
integrations.queryStripeS3BigqueryClickhouseAnd: Query Stripe, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse and other services as Postgres tables.
integrations.theRestApiPostgrestServesFor: The REST API PostgREST serves for your tables, views and functions, with generated docs.
integrations.extendTheDatabaseWithSupabaseS: Extend the database with Supabase's Postgres modules. Each one runs inside this project's stack.

integrationsQueues.durableMessageQueuesInPostgresWith: Durable message queues in Postgres with pgmq: send, read and archive messages from SQL or the API.
integrationsQueues.createsThePgmqSchemaEachQueue: Creates the pgmq schema. Each queue becomes a table of messages, plus an archive table.
integrationsQueues.name: Name
integrationsQueues.deletesAllMessagesWaitingInIt: Deletes all {{value}} messages waiting in it. The archive is kept.
integrationsQueues.dropsTheQueueItsMessagesAnd: Drops the queue, its messages and its archive. This can’t be undone.
integrationsQueues.fasterButMessagesAreLostIf: Faster, but messages are lost if Postgres crashes, and not copied to replicas.
integrationsQueues.messagesAreWrittenToTheWal: Messages are written to the WAL and survive crashes.
integrationsQueues.theFirst100MessagesOldestFirst: The first 100 messages, oldest first. Viewing them here doesn't read or hide them.

integrationsVault.secretsStoredEncryptedInTheDatabase: Secrets stored encrypted in the database. Read them in SQL from vault.decrypted_secrets, for example in cron jobs or webhooks.
integrationsVault.createsTheVaultSchemaSecretsAre: Creates the vault schema. Secrets are encrypted with a key Postgres keeps outside the database.
integrationsVault.name: Name
integrationsVault.anythingThatReadsItFromVault: Anything that reads it from vault.decrypted_secrets stops finding it. This can’t be undone.
integrationsVault.storedEncryptedAnyoneWhoCanRead: Stored encrypted. Anyone who can read vault.decrypted_secrets can read it.
integrationsVault.howSqlFindsItEG: How SQL finds it, e.g. stripe_api_key.
integrationsVault.leaveEmptyToKeepTheCurrent: Leave empty to keep the current value.

integrationsWebhooks.sendAnHttpRequestWhenRows: Send an HTTP request when rows change. Requests go out through pg_net after the transaction commits, so they never slow it down.
integrationsWebhooks.supabaseSPostgresImageCreatesIt: Supabase's Postgres image creates it when the stack first starts. Without it, webhooks have nothing to call.
integrationsWebhooks.name: Name
integrationsWebhooks.aNameOfLettersDigitsAnd: a name of letters, digits and underscores
integrationsWebhooks.postSendsTypeTableSchemaRecord: POST sends {type, table, schema, record, old_record} as JSON.
integrationsWebhooks.getSendsOnlyTheUrlThe: GET sends only the URL, the parameters and the headers; no row data.
integrationsWebhooks.reachedFromTheDatabaseContainerSo: Reached from the database container, so localhost means the database itself.
integrationsWebhooks.aJsonObjectStoredInPlain: A JSON object. Stored in plain text in the trigger definition, visible to anyone who can read the schema.
integrationsWebhooks.aJsonObjectAddedToThe: A JSON object, added to the URL as a query string.
integrationsWebhooks.theLatest50PgNetKeeps: The latest 50. pg_net keeps responses for six hours.
integrationsWebhooks.pendingOrTheResponseHasExpired: Pending, or the response has expired

integrationsWrappers.queryStripeS3BigqueryClickhouseAnd: Query Stripe, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse and other services as Postgres tables, with Supabase's foreign data wrappers.
integrationsWrappers.addsSupabaseSForeignDataWrappers: Adds Supabase's foreign data wrappers to the extensions schema. Each wrapper's credentials are kept in Vault.
integrationsWrappers.wrappersNeedVaultForTheirCredentials: Wrappers need Vault for their credentials
integrationsWrappers.wrappersKeepTheirCredentialsInVault: Wrappers keep their credentials in Vault, which isn't enabled
integrationsWrappers.enableTheSupabaseVaultExtensionTo: Enable the supabase_vault extension to add wrappers.
integrationsWrappers.thisDatabaseDoesnTHaveThe: This database doesn't have the supabase_vault extension; Supabase's own Postgres images do.
integrationsWrappers.name: Name
integrationsWrappers.dropsItAndItsForeignTable: Drops it and its foreign table
integrationsWrappers.dropsItAndItsForeignTables: Drops it and its {{length}} foreign tables
integrationsWrappers.removesTheSchemaIfNothingElse: removes the {{schema}} schema if nothing else is in it
integrationsWrappers.deletesItsCredentialsFromVaultUnless: deletes its credentials from Vault unless another wrapper uses them
integrationsWrappers.theDataStaysInThisCan: {{what}}. The data stays in {{label}}. This can’t be undone.
integrationsWrappers.pickTheServiceToQueryFrom: Pick the service to query from Postgres.
integrationsWrappers.needsWrappersOrLaterThisDatabase: Needs wrappers {{minimumExtensionVersion}} or later; this database has {{installed}}.
integrationsWrappers.vaultDidnTReturnAnId: Vault didn't return an id for {{name}}
integrationsWrappers.removingTheSecretsItHadSaved: {{value}}. Removing the secrets it had saved also failed ({{value2}}); delete {{join}} under Integrations › Vault.
integrationsWrappers.theForeignServerSNameIts: The foreign server's name. Its secrets are saved in Vault as <name>_<option>.
integrationsWrappers.importEverythingIntoANewSchema: Import everything into a new schema
integrationsWrappers.createdForTheWrapperSTables: Created for the wrapper's tables; it mustn't exist yet.
integrationsWrappers.aNewSchemaItIsCreated: A new schema; it is created first.
integrationsWrappers.thisTableSColumnsDependOn: This table's columns depend on the remote data; add the ones you want, with Postgres types.

integrationsIndex.queryTheDatabaseWithGraphqlThrough: Query the database with GraphQL through pg_graphql.

queues.useLowercaseLettersDigitsAndUnderscores: Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores

apiDocsExamples.withPaginationDescription: Rows 0 to 9. PostgREST also caps every response at its max-rows setting.
apiDocsExamples.filteringDescription: Combine filters by chaining them. Others include neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, is and in.
apiDocsExamples.upsertDescription: Inserts, or updates the row with the same primary key.
apiDocsExamples.updateDescription: Always filter an update, or every row the role can see changes.
apiDocsExamples.deleteDescription: Always filter a delete, or every row the role can see goes.
apiDocsExamples.subscribeDescription: Needs the table in the supabase_realtime publication (Database › Publications). There's no curl equivalent: Realtime uses WebSockets.
apiDocsExamples.signUpDescription: Creates a user. Unless email confirmation is off, they must confirm before signing in.
apiDocsExamples.signInWithMagicLink: Sign in with a magic link
apiDocsExamples.magicLinkDescription: Emails a sign-in link. Needs SMTP set up on the stack.
apiDocsExamples.signInWithPhoneCode: Sign in with a phone code
apiDocsExamples.phoneCodeDescription: Texts a one-time code. Needs an SMS provider set up on the stack.
apiDocsExamples.providerDescription: Redirects to an OAuth provider configured on the stack, such as GitHub.
